2. Short facts for disposal of the appeal are that, on 15-9-96 the preemptors made an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against the respondents for preemption of the transfers dated 1-9-96 and 3-9-96 vide deed Nos. 8882 and 8984 of the case land fully described in the schedules to the plaint. 

 26. In cross-examination, he however, stated that he could not remember what land of which plot or which khatian he got by way of exchange. He could not remember the date of the deed of exchange. Who was the first-party and who was the second party in the exchange deed, he could not remember. He however, denied that the exchange deed was sham and that he did not get possession of the exchanged land. He could not remember who witnessed the exchange document. He further said that the exchange deed was not read over to him nor could he have read the deed. Lastly, he denied that the exchange was fake and/or sham, he had no knowledge. 

 28. In cross-examination, he stated that the exchanged land appertained to khatian No. 40 and was 200/250 chains away from the case land. Land of khatian No. 40 comprised of 5 plots belonged to nine persons. Every one of them was owner in possession in every plot. The land belonged to Muku Mia Muku Mia was his grandfather who died leaving three sons and one daughter. One son Abdur Rab who was his father married thrice. His mother was the first wife. Abdur Rab died leaving two wives, three sons and six daughters. He denied that his two step-mothers got 14 decimals out of 54 decimals of plot No. 22 of said khatian No. 40. At present said plot No. 22 was correctly recorded in their names. His step-brothers and sisters also got land by way of inheritance. 

 32. DW 2 Fazlur Rahman also stated that before the exchange, on 15-6-95 there was an agreement for sale of the case land. He however did not file the agreement. DW-1 Mobarakullah also stated that he could not remember whether it was written in the sale deed dated 1-9-96 that on 15-6-96 he received Taka 80,000 and on receipt of rest of Taka 20,000 he executed the deed. But such agreement was recited in sale deed No. 8882 dated 1-9-96 exhibit 2. 

 37. Regarding waiver, respondent No.4 in his written objection stated that before the transfer, respondent Nos. 5 to 7 offered to sell the land to the preemptors but they expressed their inability to purchase. The vendor had not submitted any written objection against the prayer of preemption. In his examination-in-chief, respondent No. 7 as DW 1 however claimed that he ran after the preemptors to sell for five years but they ultimately declined to purchase. During cross-examination, he said that 3 months before the registration of the sale deed he offered for the last time. But he could not say the date. 

 39. DW 3 Golam Mowla however stated that at the time of talk for sale and settlement of price, he along with preemptor No. 1 (Kamal) along with GuIzar and Ruhul were present. Kamal expressed his inability to purchase.
